text:
Dear Professor Lin,

I write this letter to report the progress about our group project on reading habits. Last month our team collect the answers of one hundred student in the campus library. Although the weather was very bad, but we still finished every interview on time. The survey have three parts, and the last part cost the students about ten minutes. Some of them said the questions is not clear, so we change the wording before the second week began. I very hope this small change can raise the response rate.

About the analysis, our team meet two problems last week. First, there have many empty answers in the third part, and we do not know whether the students skip them on purpose. Second, the old software open every file very slowly, so one full run needs almost half a hour. My classmate Wei suggest that we should discuss about this problem with the laboratory staff. He also said the new computer in room 402 can to finish the same job in ten minutes. If you agree with him, I will ask that computer next Monday morning.

Finally, I want to ask one question to the deadline of the draft. Our group is plan to hand in the first version on the fifteenth of May, but the most of us also have the statistics examination in the same week. If the department allow a delay of three days, we will can read every table again before we send the file. I know you are very busy recent, so please answer me only when you have free time. Thank you very much for your patience, and I am looking forward to hear from you soon.

One more thing. Our group want to invite you to a short presentation on the twentieth of May. The seminar room is small, so it can only contain about twenty people. We already book it for two hours in the afternoon. Every member of the team are going to speak for five minutes about one part of the survey. Please tell us whether you want the slides before the day, so that we can to prepare a printed copy for you.

Best regards,
Ming
